<ROLE>
Your primary role is to assist users by executing commands, modifying code, and solving technical problems effectively. You should be thorough, methodical, and prioritize quality over speed.
* If the user asks a question, like "why is X happening", don't try to fix the problem. Just give an answer to the question.
</ROLE>

<EFFICIENCY>

* When exploring the codebase, use efficient tools like find, grep, and git commands with appropriate filters to minimize unnecessary operations.
</EFFICIENCY>

<FILE_SYSTEM_GUIDELINES>
* When a user provides a file path, do NOT assume it's relative to the current working directory. First explore the file system to locate the file before working on it.
* If asked to edit a file, edit the file directly, rather than creating a new file with a different filename.
* For global search-and-replace operations, consider using `sed` instead of opening file editors multiple times.
* NEVER create multiple versions of the same file with different suffixes (e.g., file_test.py, file_fix.py, file_simple.py). Instead:
  - Always modify the original file directly when making changes
  - If you need to create a temporary file for testing, delete it once you've confirmed your solution works
  - If you decide a file you created is no longer useful, delete it instead of creating a new version
* Do NOT include documentation files explaining your changes in version control unless the user explicitly requests it
* When reproducing bugs or implementing fixes, use a single file rather than creating multiple files with different versions
</FILE_SYSTEM_GUIDELINES>

<CODE_QUALITY>
* Write clean, efficient code with minimal comments. Avoid redundancy in comments: Do not repeat information that can be easily inferred from the code itself.
* When implementing solutions, focus on making the minimal changes needed to solve the problem.
* Before implementing any changes, first thoroughly understand the codebase through exploration.
* If you are adding a lot of code to a function or file, consider splitting the function or file into smaller pieces when appropriate.
* Place all imports at the top of the file unless explicitly requested otherwise or if placing imports at the top would cause issues (e.g., circular imports, conditional imports, or imports that need to be delayed for specific reasons).
</CODE_QUALITY>

<VERSION_CONTROL>
* If there are existing git user credentials already configured, use them and add Co-authored-by: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev> to any commits messages you make. if a git config doesn't exist use "openhands" as the user.name and "openhands@all-hands.dev" as the user.email by default, unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

* When committing changes, use `git status` to see all modified files, and stage all files necessary for the commit. Use `git commit -a` whenever possible.
* Do NOT commit files that typically shouldn't go into version control (e.g., node_modules/, .env files, build directories, cache files, large binaries) unless explicitly instructed by the user.

</VERSION_CONTROL>

<PULL_REQUESTS>

* When creating pull requests, create only ONE per session/issue unless explicitly instructed otherwise.
* When working with an existing PR, update it with new commits rather than creating additional PRs for the same issue.
* When updating a PR, preserve the original PR title and purpose, updating description only when necessary.
</PULL_REQUESTS>

<PROBLEM_SOLVING_WORKFLOW>
1. EXPLORATION: Thoroughly explore relevant files and understand the context before proposing solutions
2. ANALYSIS: Consider multiple approaches and select the most promising one

<EXTERNAL_SERVICES>

</EXTERNAL_SERVICES>

<TROUBLESHOOTING>

[ Enabling matching notifications ](#notify) 25 26 27 ## Prerequisites 28 To use this server you'll need to have a working instance of **MongoDB**. from the mongo shell you can create a database and an authenticated user to handle connections using this syntax: 29 30 ```bash 31 use pmatcher 32 db.createUser( 33 { 34 user: "pmUser", 35 pwd: "pmPassword", 36 roles: [ "dbOwner" ] 37 } 38 ) 39 ``` 40 After setting up the restricted access to the server you'll just have to launch the mongo demon using authentication: 41 ```bash 42 mongod --auth --dbpath path_to_database_data 43 ``` 44 45 46 ## Installation 47 Clone the repository from github using this command: 48 ```bash 49 git clone https://github.com/Clinical-Genomics/patientMatcher.git 50 ``` 51 52 Change directory to the cloned folder and from there install the software using the following command: 53 ```bash 54 pip install -e . 55 ``` 56 57 To customize the server configuration you'll need to edit the **config.py** file under the /instance folder.   58 For testing purposes you can keep the default configuration values as they are, but keep in mind that you should adjust these numbers when in production. 59 60 To start the server run this command: 61 ```bash 62 pmatcher run -h custom_host -p custom_port 63 ``` 64 Please note that the code is NOT guaranteed to be bug-free and it must be adapted to be used in production. 65 66 67 ## Data types 68 This server implements the [Matchmaker Exchange APIs](https://github.com/ga4gh/mme-apis). It accepts and returns patient data validated against the [json schema](https://github.com/MatchmakerExchange/reference-server/blob/master/mme_server/schemas/api.json) defined in the [MME reference-server project](https://github.com/MatchmakerExchange/reference-server). 69 70    71 72 73 ## Command line interface 74 A list of available commands can be invoked by running the following command: 75 ```bash 76 pmatcher 77 ``` 78    79 80 81 ### Adding demo data to server 82 For testing purposes you can upload a list of [50 benchmarking patients](https://github.com/ga4gh/mme-apis/tree/master/testing).  83 To add these patients to the database run the following command: 84 ```bash 85 pmatcher add demodata 86 ``` 87    88 89 90 ### Removing a patient from the database. 91 You can remove a patient using the command line interface by invoking this command and providing **either its ID or its label** (or both actually): 92 93 ```bash 94 pmatcher remove patient [OPTIONS] 95 96 Options: 97 -id TEXT ID of the patient to be removed from database 98 -label TEXT label of the patient to be removed from database 99 ``` 100    101 102 103 ### Adding a client to the database 104 In order to save patients into patientMatcher you need to create at least one authorized client.  105 Use the following command to insert a client object in the database: 106 107 ```bash 108 pmatcher add client [OPTIONS] 109 110 Options: 111 -id TEXT Client ID [required] 112 -token TEXT Authorization token [required] 113 -url TEXT Client URL [required] 114 -contact TEXT Client email 115 ``` 116 POST request aimed at adding or modifying a patient in patientMatcher **should be using a token** from a client present in the database.  117 Clients may be from the command line with this command: 118 ```bash 119 pmatcher remove client -id client_id 120 ``` 121    122 123 124 ### Adding a connected node to the database 125 To connect to another MME node and submit requests to it you should know the authentication token to the other node.  126 You can add a node to the database by running the command: 127 128 ```bash 129 pmatcher add node [OPTIONS] 130 131 Options: 132 -id TEXT Server/Client ID [required] 133 -token TEXT Authorization token [required] 134 -matching_url TEXT URL to send match requests to [required] 135 -accepted_content TEXT Accepted Content-Type [required] 136 -contact TEXT An email address 137 ``` 138 Connected nodes may be removed any time using the command:  139 ```bash 140 pmatcher remove node -id node_id 141 ``` 142    143 144 145 ## Server endpoints 146 147 148 - **/patient/add**. 149  To add patients using a **POST** request. Example: 150 ```bash 151 curl -X POST \ 152 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 153 -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.ga4gh.matchmaker.v1.0+json' \ 154 -H 'Accept: application/json' \ 155 -d '{"patient":{ 156 "id":"patient_id", 157 "contact": {"name":"Contact Name", "href":"mailto:contact_name@mail.com"}, 158 "features":[{"id":"HP:0009623"}], 159 "genomicFeatures":[{"gene":{"id":"EFTUD2"}}] 160 }}' localhost:9020/patient/add 161 ``` 162 To update the data of a patient already submitted to the server you can use the same command and add a patient with the same ID.  163 164 The action of adding or updating a patient in the server will trigger an **external search of similar patients from connected nodes**.  165 If there are no connected nodes in the database or you are uploading demo data no search will be performed on other nodes. 166 167    168 169 170 - **patient/delete/**. 171  You can delete a patient from the database by sending a **DELETE** request with its ID to the server. Example: 172 ```bash 173 curl -X DELETE \ 174 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 175 localhost:9020/patient/delete/patient_id 176 ``` 177 Please note that when a patient is deleted all its match results will be also deleted from the database. This is valid for **matches where the patient was used as the query patient** in searches performed on other nodes or the internal patientMatcher database (internal search). 178 Matching results where the removed patient is instead listed among the matching results will be not removed from the database. 179 180    181 182 183 - **/patient/view**. 184  Use this endpoint to **get** a list of all patients in the database. Example: 185 ```bash 186 curl -X GET \ 187 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 188 localhost:9020/patient/view 189 ``` 190    191 192 193 - **/nodes**. 194  **GET** the list of connected nodes. Example: 195 ```bash 196 curl -X GET \ 197 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 198 localhost:9020/nodes 199 ``` 200 The response will return a list like this : [ { 'id' : node_1_id, 'description' : node1_description }, .. ] or an empty list if the server is not connected to external nodes. 201 202    203 204 205 - **/match**. 206  **POST** a request with a query patient to patientMatcher and get a response with the patients in the server which are most similar to your query. Example: 207 ```bash 208 curl -X POST \ 209 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 210 -H 'Content-Type: application/vnd.ga4gh.matchmaker.v1.0+json' \ 211 -H 'Accept: application/vnd.ga4gh.matchmaker.v1.0+json' \ 212 -d '{"patient":{ 213 "id":"patient_id", 214 "contact": {"name":"Contact Name", "href":"mailto:contact_name@mail.com"}, 215 "features":[{"id":"HP:0009623"}], 216 "genomicFeatures":[{"gene":{"id":"EFTUD2"}}] 217 }}' localhost:9020/match 218 ``` 219 The **maximum number of patients returned by the server** is a parameter which can be customized by editing the "MAX_RESULTS" field in the config.py file. Default value is 5. 220 Patient matches are returned in order or descending similarity with the query patient (The most similar patients are higher in the list of results). 221 222    223 224 - **/match/external/**. 225  Trigger a search in external nodes for patients similar to the one specified by the ID. Example: 226 ```bash 227 curl -X POST \ 228 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 229 localhost:9020/match/external/patient_id 230 ``` 231 It is possible to search for matching patients on a specific node. To do so specify the node id in the request args. Example: 232 ```bash 233 curl -X POST \ 234 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 235 localhost:9020/match/external/patient_id?node=specific_node_id 236 ``` 237 Read [here](#node_list) how to get a list with the ID of the connected nodes. 238 239    240 241 242 - **/matches/**. 243  Return all matches (internal and external) with positive results for a patient specified by an ID. Example: 244 ```bash 245 curl -X GET \ 246 -H 'X-Auth-Token: cus...ken' \ 247 localhost:9020/matches/patient_id 248 ``` 249    250 251 252 ## Patient matching algorithm, used both for internal and external searches 253 Each patient query submitted to the server triggers a matching algorithm which will search and return those patients on the server that are most similar to the queried one. 254 Patient similarity is measured by the a **similarity score** that may span **from 0 (no matching) to 1 (exact matching)**. 255 256 Similarity score computation is taking into account **genomic similarity** and **phenotype similarity** across patients. The weight of these two factors is numerically evaluated into a GTscore and a PhenoScore, and the sum of the 2 constitutes the similarity score of the matching patient. 257 258 The relative weight of the GTscore and the PhenoScore can be customised by the database administrator by changing the values of the parameters "MAX_GT_SCORE" and "MAX_PHENO_SCORE" in the configuration file (instance/config.py). Default values are MAX_GT_SCORE: 0.5, MAX_PHENO_SCORE : 0.5. 259 260 261 ### Genotyping matching algorithm 262 GTscore is computed by evaluating the list of genomic features of the queried patient and the patients available on the MME server. 263 264 If the queried patient has no genomic features (only phenotype features) then GTscore of all the returned matches will be 0. 265 266 Example of how the algorithm works: 267 Let's assume that 0.5 is the MAX_GT_SCORE possible for a patient match (default parameters). 268 269 If for instance the queried patient (QUERY) has 3 variants, **each variant will have a relative weight** of 0.1666 (0.5/3). 0.1666 will be the maximum score for each variant. 270 Assuming having a QUERY patient with these variants: 271 - gene X variant A 272 - gene Y variant B 273 - gene Z variant C 274 275 Any patient in the database having variants in any of the X,Y,Z genes will constitute a match (MATCH) to the queried patient and will be compared against it. 276 Let's assume the variants in MATCH are: 277 - gene X variant D (1) 278 - gene Y variant B (2) 279 - gene W variant E (3) 280 281 The evaluation of the matching features is always performed on the QUERY variants, in this way: 282 - gene X variant A ---> gene match with (1). No variant match. Assigned score: 0.1666/4 (gene match only will be arbitrarily assigned a fourth of the relative weight of the variant) 283 - gene Y variant B ---> exact matching of variant and gene with (2). Assigned score: 0.1666 (max relative weight of the variant) 284 - gene Z variant C ---> No match, assigned score: 0. 285 286 GTscore assigned to the MATCH patients will then be: 0.1666/4 + 0.1666 + 0. 287 288 Note that the algorithm will evaluate and assign a score of 0.1666 (max relative weight of the variant) also to matching variants outside genes. 289 This way patients will be evaluated for genetic similarity even if the variants lay outside genes. 290 291 292 293 ### Phenotype matching algorithm 294 Phenotype similarity is calculated by taking into account **features, disorders and computed phenotypes** of a patient 295 296 - **Patient features** 297 Are specified by the eventual HPO terms provided for the query patient. **Similarity between HPO features will make up half of the maximum similarity score** between two patients. 298 299 - **Monarch phenotypes** 300 Will be computed using the [Monarch Phenotype Profile Analysis tool](https://monarchinitiative.org/analyze/phenotypes). The 5 highest scored computed phenotypes obtained by submitting a patient's HPO terms to Monarch will be used for patient matching. The similarity between computed phenotypes **will make up 1/4 of the of the maximum similarity score between two patient. For patients with no OMIM diagnosis (empty disorders field) the Monarch phenotypes will count for half of the maximum similarity score between two patient** 301 302 - **Disorders** 303 OMIM diagnoses, if available, will make up **1/4 of the maximum similarity score**. 304   305 306 307 ## Enabling match notifications 308 309 Email notification of patient matching can be enabled by editing the email notification parameters 310 in the configuration file (config.py). If you want to test your email configuration without sending real match notifications you could use this command: 311 312 ```bash 313 pmatcher test email -recipient your_email@email.com 314 ``` 315 316 Once these parameters are set to valid values a notification email will be sent in the following cases: 317 318 - A patient is added to the database and the add request triggers a search on external nodes. There is at least one returned result (/patient/add endpoint). 319 - An external search is actively performed on connected nodes and returns at least one result (/match/external/ endpoint). 320 - The server is interrogated by an external node and returns at least one match (/match endpoint). In this case a match notification is sent to each contact of the matches (patients in results). 321 - An internal search is submitted to the server using a patient from the database (/match endpoint) and this search returns at least one match. In this case contact users of all patients involved will be notified (contact from query patient and contacts from the result list of patients). 322 323 You can stop server notification any time by commenting the MAIL_SERVER parameter in config file and rebooting the server. 324 325 326 327 328 [travis-url]: https://travis-ci.org/Clinical-Genomics/patientMatcher 329 [travis-image]: https://img.shields.io/travis/Clinical-Genomics/patientMatcher.svg?style=flat-square 330
